name: GameAssist
description:
**GameAssist is a modular D&D 5E automation suite for Roll20. Its critical-miss, condition, concentration, token, NPC, reporting, configuration, and diagnostic tools support the 2014 sheet; InitiativeAssist adds mixed 2014 and 2024 initiative in Roll20's native Turn Tracker; CombatAssist provides deliberate encounter, turn, and round controls; and WelcomeAssist can open game night with a table greeting chosen by the GM.**

GameAssist v1.8.0 includes eleven individually configurable modules supported by shared, toggleable MarkerService and TurnTrackerService foundations. Guided menus and plain-language help make the common workflows approachable, while direct commands and deeper controls remain available when a campaign needs them. Every module treats its `GM` and `DM` commands as equal shortcuts to that module's primary private Game Master screen.

Campaigns upgrading from v0.1.7.0 keep their established commands, valid settings, NPC history, Arc records, and guide handouts. The canonical module names are now **CritAssist**, **NPCAssist**, **ConcentrationAssist**, and **HPAssist**; legacy command forms remain available for existing macros.

---

## âš™ï¸ Requirements

- **Roll20 access:** Mod scripts require a game created by a Roll20 Pro subscriber. Players in that game do not need their own Pro subscriptions.
- **Character sheets:** Established gameplay modules use D&D 5E by Roll20 (2014). InitiativeAssist supports both 2014 and D&D 2024 by Roll20 characters in the same encounter. Roll20's supported Experimental Mod API server may be needed for 2024 Beacon initiative data.
- **Integrated services:** Remove standalone TokenMod and StatusInfo before normal v1.8.0 use. TokenAssist and ConditionAssist provide the supported integrated replacements, and MarkerService owns their shared marker behavior.
- **NPC tokens:** NPCAssist and HPAssist use token bar 1 for HP. Tokens must be on the Objects layer, linked to a character with `npc=1`, and need `npc_hpformula` when GameAssist rolls their HP.
- **CritAssist tables:** `CF-Melee`, `CF-Ranged`, `CF-Thrown`, `CF-Spell`, `CF-Natural`, `Confirm-Crit-Martial`, and `Confirm-Crit-Magic`

> GameAssist does not invent your campaign's fumble results. Create and populate the seven rollable tables before using CritAssist table rolls.

> TokenAssist uses `!token-assist` and `!ta`/`!ta-*` commands. Older supported `!token-mod` macros continue temporarily during v1.x and should be updated before GameAssist v2.0.0. See the README for the supported command list.

---

## ğŸš€ Quick Start

GameAssist is controlled from Roll20 chat. Commands beginning with `!` are sent to Mods instead of appearing as ordinary chat messages; players do not install anything separately.

1. From the game's **Settings**, open **Mod (API) Scripts** and add **GameAssist** from the One-Click library.
2. Remove standalone TokenMod and StatusInfo so overlapping commands and marker listeners are not loaded twice.
3. Create the seven CritAssist rollable tables if you plan to use CritAssist.
4. Allow the Mod sandbox to restart, then type `!ga-status` in chat to check the installation.
5. Run `!ga-timezone` and choose the city/region that governs the campaign clock.
6. Open `!ga-config ui` and enable only the modules your campaign needs.
7. When using native initiative tools, enable **InitiativeAssist**, open Roll20's Turn Tracker, and run `!Init-Help`.
8. To track encounter turns and rounds, enable **CombatAssist**, establish initiative, then run `!Combat-Help` before starting the encounter.
9. For an optional table greeting, enable **WelcomeAssist**, run `!Welcome`, preview the result, then reload the sandbox.

Use `!Init-Help`, `!Combat-Help`, `!Welcome`, `!token-assist help`, `!condition help`, `!critfumble help`, `!concentration --help`, or `!npc-death-report --help` whenever you want an in-game guide.

## ğŸ§© Included Modules

- **CritAssist** â€” Watches supported attack templates for natural 1s, offers the attacker clear choices, and rolls from your melee, ranged, thrown, spell, or natural-attack fumble tables. The GM can also open a player picker manually or roll martial and magic confirmation tables directly.
- **ConditionAssist** â€” Uses 2014 SRD condition wording by default, offers optional 2024 SRD wording and campaign edits, and provides case-insensitive `!cond-<condition>` quick references, marker artwork, an accurate selected-token condition menu, a GM current-page condition/marker status roster, and verified marker-toggling announcements in public chat or player whispers. Valid legacy StatusInfo definitions can be copied without deleting the rollback state.
- **TokenAssist** â€” Provides `!token-assist` and `!ta`/`!ta-*` token controls for selected or authorized tokens. It handles common visibility settings, names, tooltips, bars, auras, colors, layers, position, size, rotation, vision, lighting, links, controllers, relative values, movement, stacking order, reports, and built-in or custom status markers. Marker changes always pass through MarkerService.
- **InitiativeAssist** â€” Works inside Roll20's native Turn Tracker with mixed 2014 and 2024 characters. Public initiative calls offer one-character, selected-character, and guided roll buttons while privately giving the GM object-layer and GM-layer NPC controls. `!Init-GM` and `!Init-DM` open the same neutral controls and complete roster only for the GM. NPC roll details are hidden by default, GM-layer rolls always stay private, and guided options combine d20 mode, a flat adjustment, and up to two bonus dice. `!Init-RR` whispers the GM a bounded result summary while preserving custom counters, objects, dead NPCs, mismatches, stale rows, and off-page entries.
- **CombatAssist** â€” Adds an optional encounter layer to Roll20's native Turn Tracker without replacing it. A clearly named native Round Counter can provide the authoritative round and retain its simple `+1` calculation during CombatAssist movement. The GM starts, reviews, moves forward or backward, pauses when useful, and ends tracking through a case-insensitive `!Combat-` guide. Valid combatant additions, removals, rerolls, and manual reordering preserve the current round. Optional turn timers provide stale-safe reminders without auto-advancing, and native current-turn pings add an ephemeral visual cue without changing token properties or recentering anyone's map. Private turn prompts can give the current controlling player an End My Turn button followed by a privacy-safe confirmation.
- **WelcomeAssist** â€” Starts disabled and optionally posts one delayed greeting after a healthy GameAssist startup. The GM can choose the professional greeting, the included built-in greeting library, up to ten campaign greetings, or a mixed pool that gives campaign lines double individual weight. Setup and previews stay private; automatic and explicit announcements are public.
- **ConcentrationAssist** â€” Builds normal, advantage, or disadvantage Constitution saves from damage, remembers each player's latest check, manages a concentration marker through MarkerService, and lists concentrating tokens on the page marked by Roll20's Player Ribbon.
- **NPCAssist** â€” Marks defeated NPCs, records revivals, checks HP against death markers, previews separately confirmed marker repairs, and organizes encounter history into readable handouts using **Campaign > Chapter > Section > Session** scopes. Custom Arc rosters can follow NPCs connected to a character story, vow, rivalry, investigation, redemption, or any other campaign thread. Date-managed Sessions and readable history use the DM-selected table timezone.
- **HPAssist** â€” Rolls `npc_hpformula` for selected NPCs or qualifying NPCs on the page marked by Roll20's Player Ribbon. Optional automatic rolling handles newly added tokens while setup protection prevents placeholder HP from producing false death and revival records.
- **ConfigUI** â€” Provides a GM-only chat interface for enabling modules, changing common settings, reviewing configuration, and reading module summaries. Command-based configuration remains available for advanced users.
- **DebugTools** â€” Provides optional GM-only damage, marker, and saving-throw diagnostics. DebugTools starts disabled, and every action remains a preview until the GM includes `--apply`.

## ğŸ² Example at the Table

A linked NPC falls from positive HP to 0. NPCAssist records that death in the active Campaign, Chapter, Section, and Session scopes, then asks MarkerService to apply the configured death marker. If the NPC later rises above 0 HP, GameAssist records the revival and removes the marker through the same service.

The GM can review a recent summary, audit the current page, write polished records to campaign handouts, or collect selected NPCs into a custom Arc roster. When a token needs an adjustment outside those automated workflows, TokenAssist can change the selected token without introducing a second marker system.

Before a new encounter, the GM opens Roll20's Turn Tracker and uses `!Init-Go` to invite players to roll, or `!Init-GM` / `!Init-DM` to keep the opening controls private. Players can roll one controlled character, every selected character they control, or a guided combination of d20 mode, adjustment, and bonus dice. The GM receives private controls for object-layer and GM-layer NPCs; hidden NPC modifiers and bonus dice remain GM-only. After each page-owned row is saved and verified, the appropriate audience sees the readable result. Later, `!Init-RR` can refresh every PC and living NPC without moving a round counter, object, dead creature, or attention row.

When everyone is ready, the GM starts CombatAssist. A single custom row named Round, Rounds, Round Count, Round Counter, Round Number, Round Tracker, Combat Round, or Current Round becomes the round authority; when CombatAssist moves that row to the top, a simple signed whole-number calculation such as `+1` is honored. Without one, a full uninterrupted forward cycle advances CombatAssist's internal round and a backward step never does. Optional timers can remind the GM, current player, both, or public chat without advancing initiative, while native pings can briefly identify the current token without changing it. The GM can also recover the last readable tracker, pause for several quiet edits, or use `!Combat-Next` and `!Combat-Prev` for guarded one-step movement.

### System and Configuration

- `!ga-status` â€” Show overall health, module state, errors, and dependency information
- `!ga-status --details` â€” Add activity, listener, timing, marker-service, and overlap diagnostics

- `!ga-config modules` â€” List feature modules, core services, and their current status

- `!ga-enable <ModuleOrService>` / `!ga-disable <ModuleOrService>` â€” Enable or disable a feature module or core service
- `!ga-metrics` â€” Show GameAssist runtime metrics

- `!critfumble help` â€” Open the CritAssist quick-reference guide

- `!token-assist about` or `!ta-about` â€” Review attribution, supported behavior, and current limits
- `!token-assist config` or `!ta-config` â€” Manage explicit player-ID targeting
- `!ta-on|off|flip <property...>` â€” Change supported token switches

- `!token-assist --<action> ...` â€” Use the same actions with the full command name
- `!token-mod ...` â€” Older supported syntax; replace in campaign macros before GameAssist v2.0.0

- `!Init-Roll-Selected` â€” Roll every eligible selected character controlled by the clicking GM or player
